node.statement: Apply precisely the conditional H-CB clauses. The established bijectivity and lower modulus allow the diagonal clause of conj-hcb first for h_11 and h_22, yielding bijectivity of every amplification and inverse norm <=1+C_H*e. Then apply its off-diagonal clause to h_12 with diagonal anchor h_22 and to h_21 with diagonal anchor h_11; all hypotheses were established in node 1.4.1. Together with the unconditional upper bounds this gives the two-sided estimates in node 1.4 for every j,k,n. Finally, for a level-one linear bijection h_jk, tensor algebra gives (I_n tensor h_jk)(I_n tensor h_jk^{-1})=I and the reverse product, so uniqueness of inverse gives h_jk,n^{-1}=I_n tensor h_jk^{-1}.
